description: JVM stdlib boundary slice (ISSUE-0097). JVM-only fixtures that run the real DEAL frontend (lexer → parser → name resolver → type checker) → real JvmBackend codegen → javac subprocess → java subprocess executing the emitted artifact (the harness fails a fixture whose codegen or JVM execution is bypassed). Covered forms: the stdlib modules whose declared functions use only the slice's prerequisite value types — std/console (observable stdout/stderr output), std/string (Unicode scalar-value length incl. the "héllo" 5-scalar pin, substring positions measured in Unicode scalar values with the v1.2 reference clamping (a negative start behaves as 0, a negative end yields the empty string, an end beyond the string clamps to its length), plain-text contains/startsWith/endsWith incl. the empty-part and pattern-magic-character pins, plain-text replace incl. the empty-old and %-in-replacement pins, split incl. the empty-string/empty-separator-scalar/consecutive/leading/trailing separator pins, trim with the Lua %s whitespace set), std/math (floor/ceil/sqrt/absInt/absNumber/minInt/maxInt incl. negative inputs and the extreme negative absInt, sqrt of a negative number → E8001 runtime error), std/time (nowMillis positive, recent, and second-truncated like LuaJIT's os.time() * 1000), stdlib results composing across modules, a frontend compile-error gate (E5001 wrong argument type) rejected before any backend runs, and a multi-module fixture where an imported compiled project module consumes std/string through the real orchestrator pipeline. std/table and std/json stay out of this slice (their only functions require table values) — their E6000 import rejection is pinned by JvmBackendTest.testStdlibTableBoundaryRejected.

tests.name: jvm-std-console-output
tests.description: std/console.log and std/console.error are observable on stdout and stderr (captured by the runner's merged stream)

tests.name: jvm-std-math-int
tests.description: std/math.absInt/minInt/maxInt compute on negative and positive operands, including absInt of the extreme negative safe int -9007199254740991 (every intermediate sum stays inside the safe range: small = 23, diff = g - 9007199254740968 = 23, total 46)

tests.name: jvm-std-math-sqrt-negative
tests.description: std/math.sqrt of a negative number raises E8001 'sqrt of negative number' exactly like std/math.lua — a real runtime error surfaced by executing the emitted artifact (exit 1)
tests.source:
import * as math from "std/math"
export function test(): number { return math.sqrt(-1.0); }

tests.name: jvm-std-time-nowmillis
tests.description: std/time.nowMillis() returns a positive, recent, second-truncated epoch milliseconds value (LuaJIT's os.time() * 1000 granularity — the % 1000 === 0 pin)

tests.name: jvm-std-compose
tests.description: stdlib results compose across modules: str.length feeds math.absInt, str.trim feeds str.contains, and the observable console output pins both paths
